title: Pattern Matching (Part 1) - Enum variants
learning_objectives: Define an enum with both simple and data-carrying variants.
Use a `match` expression that handles every variant.
Destructure carried values inside match arms to build a response.
explanation: This slice introduces pattern matching through a single enum. The key idea is that `match` is exhaustive: every variant must be handled, and any data carried by a variant can be unpacked right inside the arm that handles it.

examples.title: Define enum variants with attached data
Match and destructure every variant
Compare with a guarded integer match

completion_criteria: Exercise tests cover every enum variant, including variants with carried data
Learner can explain why the compiler rejects a non-exhaustive match
Learner can identify which values are destructured in each match arm
